decisions.quote: The utility value interventions utilized in the current studies were based on the self-generated utility value interventions used by Hulleman and colleagues (e.g., Hulleman et al., 2010; Hulleman & Harackiewicz, 2009). In addition to replicating this prior research, we extend it in five ways.
decisions.reason: The paper collects new data in a randomized classroom experiment (Study 2) to re-test the previously published utility value intervention findings, which is a replication.

decisions.quote: Although the research generated by the expectancy-value framework has been largely correlational (Wigfield & Cambria, 2010), recent classroom studies reveal that interventions designed to enhance perceptions of value can increase both interest and course perfor- mance (e.g., Hulleman & Harackiewicz, 2009; Hulleman, Godes, Hendricks, & Harackiewicz, 2010). The research presented herein replicates and extends this prior work by further investigating a theory-based intervention designed to enhance student motivation and performance.
decisions.reason: Both shipped row 91 and blind target 0 correctly identify Hulleman & Harackiewicz (2009) (DOI: 10.1126/science.1177067), which is explicitly cited as a target re-tested by Study 2.

decisions.quote: The results of Study 2 partially replicated prior research dem- onstrating that a theoretically guided intervention based on the expectancy-value framework could enhance student learning out- comes (Hulleman & Harackiewicz, 2009; Hulleman et al., 2010).
decisions.reason: While the intervention replicated the positive effects on interest and performance for low-performing students mentioned in the abstract, the authors explicitly state an overall verdict in the Study 2 Discussion that their results 'partially replicated prior research' (Hulleman & Harackiewicz, 2009; Hulleman et al., 2010) because the intervention failed to increase perceived utility value or mediate outcomes via utility value as found in both original studies, acting through success expectancies instead.
